steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Ionian Revolt (499-494 BC) was a rebellion of Greek city-states in Asia Minor against Persian rule

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Aristagoras, tyrant of Miletus, initiated the revolt after a failed attack on Naxos left him fearing Persian punishment

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Athens sent 20 ships and Eretria sent 5 to support the Ionians — this enraged King Darius

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The burning of Sardis (498 BC) was the revolt's greatest success but provoked a devastating Persian response
